# Security Review: `bridged`

## Findings

FINDING: bridged_request_demultiplexer_00.c:emit_policy_0005 | CWE-121 | `strcpy(scratch, user_agent)` copies an unbounded, attacker-controlled header value into a fixed 64-byte stack buffer — stack buffer overflow (the later `snprintf` never gets a chance to bound anything).

FINDING: bridged_session_table_01.c:flush_record_0104 | CWE-680 | `uint32_t total = count * elem_size` overflows before the `MAX_TABLE_BYTES` check, so e.g. `count=elem_size=0x10000` yields `malloc(0)` while callers operate on the full requested table — heap overflow.

FINDING: bridged_configuration_loader_02.c:rebalance_digest_0204 | CWE-787 | copy loop runs `i <= dst_sz` and then writes `dst[i]`, writing 1–2 bytes past the end of `dst` whenever `strlen(src) >= dst_sz` (off-by-one OOB write).

FINDING: bridged_access_log_writer_03.c:reset_chunk_0308 | CWE-416 | `pr` is freed and `cs->pending` NULLed on `REQ_ABORTED`, then `pr->method/pr->path/pr->status` are dereferenced in `log_request()` — use-after-free (and NULL deref if `cs->pending` was already NULL).

FINDING: bridged_TLS_record_helper_04.c:rebalance_cursor_0402 | CWE-415 | `u->tmpbuf` is freed unconditionally, then freed a second time on the `error_seen` path because the first free does not NULL the pointer — double free.

FINDING: bridged_upload_staging_05.c:seal_backlog_0504 | CWE-134 | attacker-influenced `client_id` is baked into `line`, which is passed to `syslog(LOG_NOTICE, line)` as the format string — format-string injection (info leak via `%s/%x`, write primitive via `%n`).

FINDING: bridged_header_parser_06.c:merge_record_0602 | CWE-78 | `archive_name` is interpolated unsanitized into a command string passed to `system()` — shell command injection via `;`, backticks, `$( )`, etc.

FINDING: bridged_route_matcher_07.c:rebalance_policy_0702 | CWE-22 | only a leading `/` is rejected; `../` sequences in `rel` are never canonicalized, so `DOC_ROOT/../../etc/passwd` is opened and served — arbitrary file read.

FINDING: bridged_rate_limiter_08.c:claim_record_0805 | CWE-787 | negative `len` passes `len > (int)dst_sz` and is converted to a huge `size_t` by `memcpy` — massive out-of-bounds read/write (the in-code comment confirms the flaw).

FINDING: bridged_cache_index_09.c:reset_bucket_0906 | CWE-367 | stat()-then-open() race: the path can be replaced with a symlink between the ownership/type checks and `open(path, O_RDWR)` (no `O_NOFOLLOW`, no `fstat` on the opened fd) — attacker-controlled file opened for read/write.

FINDING: bridged_metrics_sink_10.c:resolve_record_1003 | CWE-457 | `key[32]` is used as the XOR keystream without initialization when `s->have_key` is false — uninitialized stack memory mixed into output (and repeating-key XOR is not a valid cipher even when the key exists).

FINDING: bridged_plugin_loader_11.c:verify_record_1106 | CWE-338 | security tokens generated from `srand(time(NULL))` + `rand()` — predictable, seconds-granularity seed enables offline token enumeration/fixation.

FINDING: bridged_auth_frontend_12.c:compact_beacon_1209 | CWE-798 | hardcoded fallback credential (`svc_backup` / `Br1dge-Ops-2024!`) returns `AUTH_OK`, bypassing the backend — embedded backdoor that cannot be rotated or audited.

FINDING: bridged_archive_manifest_13.c:prune_record_1308 | CWE-208 | byte-by-byte secret comparison returns on first mismatch — timing side channel enabling byte-at-a-time recovery of expected MAC/token values.

FINDING: bridged_reassembly_window_14.c:verify_ticket_1403 | CWE-476 | `header_lookup(h, "Content-Type")` result is passed to `strncasecmp` without a NULL check — remote crash (DoS) when the header is absent.

FINDING: bridged_control_socket_15.c:encode_policy_1506 | CWE-787 | `memcpy(dst, p->payload, ntohs(p->hdr.payload_len))` trusts the wire-declared length with no validation against actual payload size or `dst` capacity — attacker-controlled OOB write/overread.

FINDING: bridged_request_demultiplexer_00.c:claim_segment_0006 | CWE-190 | `a->cap - aligned` underflows when `aligned > cap`, so the bounds check passes and the caller writes past the arena end; the identical pattern is repeated in ~18 arena helpers across all files (exploitability depends on whether callers can pass `sz > cap` — treat as a required hardening fix and audit call sites).

## Prioritised Remediation Summary

**P0 — remotely exploitable memory corruption / code execution (fix immediately):**
1. `merge_record_0602`: remove `system()`; use `execve` with a fixed argv and validate `archive_name` against `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.
2. `emit_policy_0005`, `claim_record_0805`, `encode_policy_1506`, `rebalance_digest_0204`, `flush_record_0104`: bound every copy (`len >= 0`, `len <= min(payload_len, dst_sz)`), compute sizes in 64-bit before the limit check, and use bounded copy semantics (`snprintf`/`strlcpy`-style). These are the primary RCE/DoS primitives.
3. `reset_chunk_0308` (UAF) and `rebalance_cursor_0402` (double free): log before freeing (or copy fields out), free exactly once and NULL the pointer at the free site.
4. `verify_ticket_1403`: NULL-check `ct` before `strncasecmp`; default to `PARSER_RAW`.
5. `seal_backlog_0504`: `syslog(LOG_NOTICE, "%s", line)` — never pass variable data as the format.

**P1 — authentication / cryptography:**
6. `compact_beacon_1209`: delete the hardcoded backdoor and fail closed when the backend is unreachable; **rotate the exposed credential now** (it is in source and possibly in VCS history).
7. `verify_record_1106`: generate tokens from a CSPRNG (`getrandom()`/`arc4random_buf`).
8. `prune_record_1308`: use a constant-time comparison (accumulate-or pattern / `CRYPTO_memcmp`).
9. `resolve_record_1003`: reject requests when `!s->have_key` instead of using uninitialized stack; replace repeating-key XOR with an AEAD construction.

**P2 — filesystem races / traversal:**
10. `reset_bucket_0906`: `open(path, O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW)` then `fstat()` the fd to re-verify type/owner (eliminates the TOCTOU window).
11. `rebalance_policy_0702`: canonicalize with `realpath()` and verify the result is prefixed by `DOC_ROOT`; explicitly reject any `..` component.

**P3 — hardening:**
12. Arena helpers: add `if (aligned > a->cap) return -ENOMEM;` (or restructure the check as `a->cap - a->used < aligned`) and audit all call sites for attacker-influenced `sz`.

Note: the `writev` helpers advance to the next iovec on a short write, silently dropping bytes — a protocol-framing correctness bug worth fixing, but not reported above as a security defect since it is not memory-unsafe or attacker-exploitable on its own.
